knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r setup}
library(totalevalerror)
```

This vignette replicates the AILuminate safety analysis from Messing (2026, Section `sec:safety`) on the bundled `safety_pilot` subsample. The headline is that the dominant variance source is item x judge interaction, and that swapping a single judge for three judges reduces the SE substantially.

## 1. Load the pilot

```{r load}
data(safety_pilot)
str(safety_pilot)

des <- tee_design(
  safety_pilot,
  outcome     = outcome,
  item        = item_id,
  category    = category,
  prompt      = variant_id,
  judge       = judge_model,
  temperature = temperature,
  replicate   = replication,
  scoring     = "binary"
)
```

## 2. LPM and GLMM decompositions

```{r fit}
fit_lpm <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  tee_decompose(des, link = "identity")
))
generics::tidy(fit_lpm)[, c("tle_label", "variance", "pct_total", "tier")]
```

## 3. Naive vs TEE SE

```{r naive}
naive <- tee_naive_se(des)
tee_se_compare(fit_lpm, naive)
```

## 4. What does swapping 1 judge for 3 buy us?

```{r swap_judges}
tee_se(fit_lpm, M = 1L, fix_judge = TRUE)
tee_se(fit_lpm, M = 3L, fix_judge = FALSE)
```

## 5. Per-category D-study

```{r per_cat, eval = FALSE}
# Per-category D-study refits the model on each category subset and stacks
# the projections. Skipped here because the bundled subsample is small;
# enable on the full data for category-level guidance.
proj_cat <- tee_dstudy(fit_lpm, by = "category")
head(proj_cat$scenarios)
```

## 6. Auto-paragraph

```{r writeup, results = "asis"}
cat(tee_writeup(fit_lpm, style = "paper"))
```
